title: Fast-path: High-velocity enterprise security ask triage and pre-approved evidence bundles
creator: Lena Chen
description:
Summary:
Create a lightweight 'Fast-path' lane for recurring enterprise security and compliance requests coming from high-velocity accounts (e.g., committed spend, strategic pilots, or CSM-led trials). The lane should reduce time-to-response by combining: (1) an automated intake scorer for questionnaire complexity, (2) pre-approved evidence bundles (DPA, SOC2 excerpts, encryption/KMS attestation, data residency statements), and (3) templated answers for frequently-asked vendor questionnaire items. The goal is to triage and either auto-respond or route to the appropriate SME within 48 hours for >80% of qualifying requests.

Context and motivation:
Sales/CS teams are spending disproportionate time assembling the same artifacts for many enterprise deals. Current intake is manual and routed to Security or Legal every time, causing 3–10 day delays. Creating a fast-path will improve win rates, reduce CSM time spent, and limit Legal/InfoSec overhead to high-complexity exceptions. This complements the broader compliance-intake work (see PM-23109) but focuses on velocity and repeatability for a subset of accounts.

Scope (in-scope):
- Intake form enhancement with eligibility flags (contract signed, MRR threshold, pilot status).
- Automated questionnaire classifier that assigns complexity score (low/medium/high).
- A curated library of pre-approved evidence bundles and templated answers for the top 120 questionnaire items.
- Self-serve evidence portal for CSMs to download curated bundles.
- Routing and SLA rules: auto-respond for low complexity; 48h SME response for medium; full Legal/InfoSec review for high.

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Full overhaul of vendor questionnaire engine (future phase).
- Changes to SMR encryption or new certs.

Trade-offs and design notes:
- Automation vs. risk: pre-approved bundles accelerate response but must be guarded by policy (which fields can be auto-sent). We will restrict auto-answers to vetted, low-risk items; anything involving custom security commitments or data residency exceptions goes to Legal.
- Accuracy vs. coverage: classifier tuned for precision initially to avoid false auto-responses; this reduces automation percentage early but minimizes risk.
- UX friction vs. adoption: keep form minimal for CSMs; leverage SFDC flags to reduce duplication.

Proposed rollout phases:
1) Phase 1 (MVP, 4 weeks): build eligibility flags, simple rule engine, 3 pre-approved bundles (SOC2 summary + report access workflow, standard DPA redline, encryption and KMS attestation), and a CSM downloads page. Metrics: triage time, % auto-marked low complexity.
2) Phase 2 (8 weeks): questionnaire classifier (ML-lite), templated answers for top 120 items, automated draft responses for CSM review, integrations with Zendesk + SFDC.
3) Phase 3 (quarter 2): expand bundles, analytics in Console for intake latency, feedback loop to expand auto-answer coverage.

Key success metrics:
- Mean time to initial triage cut from current baseline to <= 48 hours for qualifying accounts.
- % of qualifying requests auto-responded or resolved without Legal/InfoSec review >= 60 at 3 months.
- CSM time saved per closed deal (hours).
- Reduction in Legal ticket volume from repeat requests.

Stakeholders and reviewers:

- Sales/CS lead: Aisha Kapoor

- Legal: Priya Raman
- Eng lead: Ravi Singh
- Design: Elena Morales

Links to artifacts:
- PRD (working): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENT/Fast-Path+Security+Ask+PRD
- Design mocks (CSM portal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/fast-path-designs
- Prototype intake form (Figma): https://www.figma.com/file/fast-path-intake
- Placeholder GH spec for classifier: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eng-policies/pull/1234

Operational considerations:
- Evidence bundles must be stored in a locked S3 bucket with access logs and RBAC; CSM download events are audited.
- Versioned evidence: bundles should have a version and 'last-reviewed' metadata to ensure we don't send stale artifacts.
- SLA commitments must be surfaced to Sales/CS dashboards; automated escalation if 48h breached.

Risk and mitigation:
- Risk: incorrect auto-answers leak contractual commitments. Mitigation: conservative whitelist of auto-answerable items and a mandatory legal approval step for any novel clause.
- Risk: CSMs bypass the fast-path and continue ad-hoc asks. Mitigation: education, SFDC workflow enforcement, and analytics to show time savings.

Next steps:
- Align stakeholders in a 60-minute kickoff (target 2026-03-15).
- Eng spike to validate classifier feasibility (2 sprint-days).
- Legal to draft pre-approved evidence template language.
acceptance_criteria: Eligibility flags implemented and persisted on intake records
Three pre-approved evidence bundles live and downloadable from CSM portal
Rule engine routes low complexity requests to auto-respond flow
Automated draft responses created for medium complexity items and visible in Zendesk ticket
Metrics dashboard tracks triage time and % auto-resolved requests
